title: XaaS Containers: Performance-Portable Representation With Source and IR Containers
problem: Containers provide portability but sacrifice hardware-specific optimizations in HPC environments. Current containerization approaches force early-stage compilation decisions that limit performance across diverse HPC systems.
motivation: HPC systems and cloud data centers are converging on container-based deployment, but portable containers cannot achieve peak performance due to ABI compatibility constraints and inability to adapt to target hardware specifications.
method: The approach packages code in two flexible forms—source code (human-readable) and intermediate representation (a half-compiled form)—inside containers. Rather than making hardware-specific optimization choices when building the container, it waits until deployment time. When the container lands on a specific machine, AI models automatically discover which optimizations work best for that hardware and compile the code accordingly, keeping everything inside the container.
key_novelty: The system keeps code in flexible form inside containers and delays hardware-specific optimization decisions until deployment time, when AI automatically discovers the best optimizations for the target hardware.
contributions: XaaS container architecture combining source and IR representations for performance portability
LLM-assisted automatic discovery of specialization opportunities
Methodology for system-specialized container builds at deployment time
Prototype demonstration combining containerization convenience with performance benefits of specialized builds

metrics.performance_portability: Peak performance across all HPC systems
metrics.overhead: Container convenience with specialized build performance

limitations: Abstract only; no explicit performance benchmarks provided; assumes applicability across HPC software spectrum
